fiction.description: Invented stories, even when inspired by real events.

non-fiction.description: Works presented as factual, rather than invented stories.

fantasy.description: Stories with magic, supernatural worlds or beings.

science-fiction.description: Speculative stories about science, technology or imagined futures.

mystery.description: A puzzle, unexplained event or crime drives the story.

thriller.description: Tension, danger and suspense drive the story.

horror.description: Stories intended to create fear or dread.

romance.description: A central romantic relationship drives the story.

drama.description: Character conflict and emotional relationships drive the story.

action.description: Physical conflict, chases or combat are prominent.

adventure.description: Journeys, quests, exploration or daring challenges.

history.description: Past events, societies or historical inquiry are central subjects. This does not establish whether a work is fiction or nonfiction, or identify a particular period.
history.label: History

humor.description: Comedy or amusement is a significant part of the work.
humor.label: comedy/humor

sports.description: Athletic competition, training or teams are central.

biography.description: Factual accounts exploring the lives, experiences, relationships, achievements, and historical or cultural significance of real people.

memoir.description: A personal account of selected life experiences.

popular-science.description: Science explained for a general audience.

true-crime.description: Factual accounts of crimes and investigations.

nature.description: Wildlife, ecosystems or the natural world are central subjects, in fiction or nonfiction.
nature.label: Nature

travel.description: Travel, journeys or experiences of places are central subjects, in factual accounts or fiction.
travel.label: Travel

politics.description: Government, political institutions, public policy or political power are central subjects.
politics.label: Politics

philosophy.description: Questions of knowledge, ethics, existence or reasoning are central subjects.
philosophy.label: Philosophy

arts.description: Art, artists and creative practices are central subjects, whether presented factually or through fiction.
arts.label: Art

technology.description: Technological systems, inventions or their effects on society are central subjects.
technology.label: Technology

epic-fantasy.description: Large-scale fantasy conflicts and richly developed imagined worlds.

urban-fantasy.description: Magic or supernatural beings in a modern urban setting.

dark-fantasy.description: Fantasy with disturbing, bleak or horror elements.

mythic-fantasy.description: Fantasy drawing on myths, gods or legendary beings.

fairy-tales.description: Traditional or reimagined tales involving enchantment and folklore.

magical-realism.description: An otherwise ordinary world presents extraordinary events as everyday life.

space-opera.description: Large-scale adventures and conflicts across space.

cyberpunk.description: Advanced technology alongside social inequality, often in urban settings.

time-travel.description: Moving between different times is central.

dystopian.description: An oppressive or deeply troubled imagined society.

first-contact.description: An initial encounter between humanity and extraterrestrial life.

cozy-mystery.description: A mystery emphasizing community and investigation with limited graphic violence.

detective-fiction.description: Fiction centered on investigators who use clues, observation, evidence or deduction to solve mysteries, with the investigative process central to the narrative.

police-procedural.description: The methods and teamwork of police investigations are central.

psychological-thriller.description: Suspense focused on perception, motives and mental conflict.

crime-thriller.description: Suspense-driven fiction centered on criminal activity, investigations, or the pursuit of criminals.

spy-thriller.description: Espionage, intelligence work and secrecy drive suspense.

gothic-horror.description: Atmospheric horror involving isolation, secrets or ominous settings.

supernatural-horror.description: Fear centered on forces beyond ordinary explanation.

cosmic-horror.description: Fear of vast, incomprehensible forces and human insignificance.

historical-romance.description: A central love story set in the past.

contemporary-romance.description: A central love story in a contemporary setting.

paranormal-romance.description: A love story involving supernatural beings or powers.

romantic-comedy.description: A romantic story with a strong comedic focus.

historical-fiction.description: An invented story set in a recognizable past period.

family-drama.description: Conflict and relationships within a family.

sports-drama.description: A character-driven drama centered on sport.

satire.description: Humor or irony used to criticize institutions or behavior.

political-biography.description: An account of a real person’s life focused on political activity.

scientific-biography.description: An account of a real scientist’s life and work.

artist-biography.description: An account of a real artist’s life and creative work.

travel-memoir.description: A personal recollection organized around real journeys.

family-memoir.description: A personal recollection focused on real family relationships and history.

astronomy.description: Celestial bodies, astronomical observation or the study of the universe are central subjects; a space setting alone is insufficient.
astronomy.label: Astronomy

psychology.description: Mind, behavior or mental processes are central subjects; this does not by itself imply psychological thriller.
psychology.label: Psychology

natural-history.description: Organisms, ecosystems and the development of the natural world are central subjects.
natural-history.label: Natural history

personal-growth.description: Practical guidance intended to support personal development.

productivity.description: Practical guidance about organizing time and completing work.

animation.description: Works created wholly or substantially through animated imagery.

anime.description: Japanese animation, or works explicitly classified as anime by the source.

donghua.description: Chinese animation, distinct from Japanese anime and live-action Chinese dramas.

manga.description: Japanese comics told through sequential art; individual volumes belong to a larger work when series metadata is available.

light-novel.description: A Japanese prose publishing format, often illustrated; distinct from manga.

sports-anime.description: Anime centered on athletic competition, teams or training.

short-film.description: A work explicitly identified as a short film; not inferred from a guessed duration.

limited-series.description: A television work identified as a limited or miniseries.

novella.description: A prose work identified by its source as a novella.

book-series.description: A book belongs to a named collection of related volumes. This compatibility label does not establish volume order; series identity and position should be stored separately.

friendship.description: Bonds between friends matter to the story.

found-family.description: People form family-like bonds beyond biological relations.

identity.description: Questions of who a person is or belongs with.

self-discovery.description: Learning about one’s identity, values or desires.

revenge.description: Seeking retaliation for a perceived wrong.

rebellion.description: Resistance against authority or an established order.

magic.description: Supernatural powers, spells or enchantment are central to the fictional work. Stage illusion or factual study of magical beliefs does not by itself qualify.

hidden-world.description: A secret world exists alongside ordinary life.

good-versus-evil.description: A conflict framed around opposing moral forces.

basketball.description: Basketball players, teams, training or competition are central subjects.
basketball.label: Basketball

football.description: A football code is central, but the available metadata does not distinguish association football, American football or another code. Do not assume which code is meant.
football.label: Football (unspecified code)

baseball.description: Baseball players, teams, training or competition are central subjects.
baseball.label: Baseball

competition.description: Rivalry or contests are central to the subject or story.

teamwork.description: Cooperation among people pursuing a shared goal.

political-intrigue.description: Power struggles, alliances and political maneuvering.

power-and-corruption.description: How authority is exercised, abused or resisted.

quest.description: A journey to accomplish an important goal.

coming-of-age.description: Growing maturity, identity and the transition toward adulthood.

superheroes.description: Characters with extraordinary abilities undertaking heroic roles.

martial-arts.description: Martial disciplines, training, practice or their history are central subjects, in fiction or nonfiction.
martial-arts.label: Martial arts

trust-and-betrayal.description: Trust, deception and broken loyalties are central.

discovery-and-innovation.description: Developing or uncovering new knowledge, tools or ideas.

chosen-one.description: A character singled out for a special destiny.

learning-magic.description: A character studies or trains to use magical abilities.

marriage-of-convenience.description: A marriage begins for practical reasons rather than love.

forbidden-love.description: A central romance faces social or external prohibitions.

second-chance-romance.description: Former partners have another opportunity at romance.

enemies-to-lovers.description: An antagonistic relationship develops into romance.

friends-to-lovers.description: An established friendship develops into romance.

fake-relationship.description: Characters pretend to be in a relationship.

slow-burn.description: A romantic relationship develops gradually over the story.

solving-a-mystery.description: Uncovering the explanation of an unknown event drives the plot.

locked-room-mystery.description: A crime appears impossible because access or escape seems blocked.

amateur-sleuth.description: A nonprofessional investigator takes the central detective role.

heist.description: Planning or carrying out a significant theft drives the plot.

unreliable-narrator.description: The narration cannot be accepted as a dependable account.

race-against-time.description: A deadline creates urgency for the central goal.

family-secrets.description: Hidden family information shapes the story or account.

magical-school.description: A school where magic is learned.

school.description: A school or academy is a significant setting.

small-town.description: A small community forms the setting.

workplace.description: A place of employment forms a significant setting.

space.description: A substantial part of the depicted events takes place in outer space or aboard a spacecraft. Discussing astronomy alone does not establish this setting.

royal-court.description: A royal household and its surrounding society form the setting.

imperial-court.description: An emperor’s household and its surrounding society form the setting.

medieval.description: A setting in a medieval period.

second-world-war.description: A setting during the Second World War.

lighthearted.description: A generally playful or low-intensity tone.

heartwarming.description: A tone emphasizing affection, kindness or reassurance.

suspenseful.description: A tone of uncertainty and anticipation.

hope.description: An emotional atmosphere emphasizing the possibility of a better future; distinct from merely discussing hope as an idea.
hope.label: Hopeful

dark.description: A bleak, disturbing or grim emotional atmosphere.

bittersweet.description: Positive feelings are mixed with sadness or loss.

melancholic.description: A sustained atmosphere of sadness or reflection.

tense.description: A sustained sense of pressure or unease.

uplifting.description: An encouraging or emotionally restorative atmosphere.

children.description: Works primarily intended for children according to source or editorial audience information. This is not a content-safety rating or age-verification result.

middle-grade.description: A publishing audience category typically aimed at children around ages 8–12; not a safety rating.

young-adult.description: A publishing audience category typically aimed at teens; not a safety rating.

adult-audience.description: Intended for adult readers or viewers; does not imply explicit content.

all-ages.description: Works intended for a broad range of ages according to source or editorial information; not a guarantee of suitability for every child.

comedy-humor.description: Archived duplicate of the active humor tag, whose display name is comedy/humor. Retained for compatibility with older saved records.
comedy-humor.label: comedy/humor

crime.description: Works centered on criminal activity, investigations, or the consequences of crime.
crime.label: crime

war.description: Armed conflict and its effects on people, communities or societies are central to the work.
war.label: war

western.description: Stories drawing on frontier life and Western genre conventions, commonly involving settlement, law, conflict or life on a frontier.
western.label: western

religious.description: Religious beliefs, practices, institutions or spiritual traditions are central subjects. This does not imply an inspirational tone.
religious.label: Religion

documentary.description: A screen work presented primarily as a factual account of real people, events or subjects; the label does not independently verify every claim.
documentary.label: documentary

family.description: Family relationships, kinship or family life are central subjects; this does not mean family-friendly content.
family.label: Family

musical.description: A narrative work in which songs and musical performances are integral to the storytelling, rather than merely background music.
musical.label: musical

reality-tv.description: Television structured around real participants and ostensibly unscripted events, which may be edited, staged or produced.
reality-tv.label: reality tv

game-show.description: A program structured around participants playing games or completing competitive challenges.
game-show.label: game show

talk-show.description: A program structured around interviews, discussion or conversation with hosts and guests.
talk-show.label: talk show

soap-opera.description: An ongoing serialized drama emphasizing interconnected personal relationships and continuing conflicts.
soap-opera.label: soap opera

sitcom.description: An episodic comedy built around recurring characters and a familiar social or domestic situation.
sitcom.label: sitcom

medical-mystery.label: Medical mystery
medical-mystery.description: Mystery fiction in which investigating an unexplained illness, diagnosis, poisoning or other medical puzzle is central to the story. A medical setting or a character who practices medicine alone is not sufficient.
